text:
maya: FYI running into a repeatable flake on Android SDK when retries kick in. POST with streaming RequestBody fails on retry (server sees empty body).

sam: ugh yeah that sounds like the classic non-repeatable RequestBody issue with OkHttp. Is this the sdk client retries or Retrofit/OkHttp internal?

maya: SDK has an internal retry interceptor for 5xx/connection resets. The first attempt is fine, but retries send a zero-length payload. Happens mostly on devices/emulator, sometimes CI.

ajules: can you paste a minimal repro? is it multipart/streamed chunked, or using RequestBody.create?

maya: repro: streaming upload via RequestBody where writeTo() reads an InputStream. On retry OkHttp reuses the Request object and RequestBody but InputStream has been consumed. Server returns 400.

axel: classic. OkHttp won't rewind your stream for you. Two common fixes: buffer body in memory (or temp file) so writeTo can be replayed, or disable automatic retries for requests with non-repeatable bodies.

sam: for Android that's rough on mobile (memory). Did you try using okio Buffer to copy into a buffered RequestBody?

maya: Tried a Buffer but worried about large attachments. Here is what I tried:
```
class ReplayableRequestBody(private val source: InputStream) : RequestBody() {
  private val buffer = Buffer()
  override fun contentType(): MediaType? = "application/octet-stream".toMediaTypeOrNull()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    if (buffer.size == 0L) {
      buffer.readFrom(source)
    }
    sink.writeAll(buffer.clone())
  }
}
```

jules: buffer.clone() is expensive but works. Problem: readFrom(source) will fully load input into RAM. For large files use File-backed temp buffer (okio.SegmentedFile or temp File + sink).

axel: another approach: have the SDK mark the request as non-retriable when RequestBody declares streaming. Expose a flag like retryOnUnrepeatableBodies=false by default for mobile. That keeps mobile memory low.

sam: Agreed. SDK parity note: our Node/Python SDKs already treat streaming bodies as non-retriable. Kotlin/Java should mirror that behavior.

maya: I can put a PR that: (1) detects when RequestBody uses InputStream (heuristic) and disables retry for that request, (2) adds an optional ReplayableRequestBody util for customers who opt in. Thoughts?

jules: +1 for opt-in util. Also add docs in SDK onboarding: "If you use streaming bodies, either provide a repeatable RequestBody or disable retries." Clear guidance will save support tickets.

axel: Also add an integration test on emulator that simulates connection reset after first attempt and asserts no empty-body request on retry. Catches regressions.

maya: Good call. One more Android quirk: HttpURLConnection fallback on older devices exposes chunking difference that can trip some servers. We already have a test harness, but let's include a small sample in mobile samples repo.

sam: For sample code, maybe show a small disk-backed ReplayableBody: use File.createTempFile() + Okio.sink(file) then write the stream once and replay from File. Less memory, predictable.

maya: I'll draft PR and sample. Plan: disable auto-retry for streaming bodies in 0.9.3, add docs sample and a utility class in 0.9.4. Targeting next week for draft.

devbot: reminder: create a ticket for QA tests and update changelog.

jules: Thanks maya — please tag me on the PR, I'll review for API parity with Python/Node and add docs changes. :+1:

sam: If you want, I can sketch the temp-file ReplayableBody this afternoon and attach to the PR.

maya: awesome, that would speed it up. I'll open the draft PR and link the failing CI run.

axel: Also add a note in release notes: "Important: Requests with streaming bodies are now opt-out of retries" so users don't get surprised.

maya: noted. Thanks all.
